(CNN) — If you’re planning a vacation in Miami, it makes sense to stay close to the sand and surf — and luckily, that’s also where many of the city’s most stylish hotels can be found.

South Beach is famous for its eye-catching Art Deco hotels, including The Delano. Many of these distinctive buildings were constructed during the 1920s and 1930s and are often finished in vivid pastel shades. Since the 1970s, South Beach’s original Art Deco structures have been protected, and a large number have since been restored to an extremely high standard.

Collins Avenue has an especially strong concentration of boutique hotels. The Delano, at 1685 Collins Avenue, offers double rooms from $400. Built in the 1940s, it features sleek fin-like details that are unmistakably Deco. Ian Schrager has reinvented the property, giving it a chic, minimalist white interior designed by Philippe Starck. Its Rose Bar is among Miami’s best spots for enjoying a cocktail beside the pool.

Another Deco property brought back to life by Schrager is The Shore Club, at 1901 Collins Avenue, where doubles start at $300. If anything, it may be even trendier than The Delano. The rooms are comfortable, technologically advanced and frequently host visiting celebrities. Nobu, the hotel’s sushi restaurant, is excellent, while the fashionable Skybar — complete with four bars and lush tropical gardens — ranks among the city’s most popular nightlife destinations.

Do you have a preferred hotel or favorite place to stay in Miami?

For those with lottery-winner budgets, the Setai, at 2001 Collins Avenue, has double rooms beginning at $785. It is another Art Deco hotel conversion, though this one has been expanded with a 40-story tower and incorporates elegant Asian design elements. Inside, the atmosphere is dark, cool and refined — a welcome contrast to the excesses of South Beach. It is openly extravagant and extremely costly.

For a more down-to-earth option, The Standard, at 40 Island Avenue in Miami Beach, offers doubles from $250. Its position on Biscayne Bay leaves it feeling a little isolated, but it represents strong value. The highlight is the excellent spa, which includes an infinity pool and an outdoor mud lounge. Still, this is not a strict or solemn wellness retreat; it is easygoing, enjoyable and better because of that. This is Miami, after all.

A less expensive and more eccentric choice is the Pelican, at 826 Ocean Drive, where doubles start at $200. Owned by the Italian fashion brand Diesel, the hotel is bright, playful and kitschy, with rooms decorated around individual themes — including the elaborate, flower-filled “Power Flower” room. Its Pelican Café has an impressive wine selection and is surprisingly affordable.

If you’re willing to stay away from the beach entirely, the Biltmore, at 1200 Anastasia Avenue in Coral Gables, is a real treasure. Double rooms begin at $310. The guest rooms themselves are not especially remarkable, but the building is magnificent, inspired by the Giralda bell tower in Seville and decorated with ornate Moorish-style details. Al Capone was a devoted admirer in the 1920s. Today, the hotel features a huge swimming pool, an 18-hole golf course and stories of ghosts said to live there.

Miami’s most glamorous hotels are clustered close to the ocean, with the greatest concentration found in South Beach and along Collins Avenue. This part of the city has long been associated with style, nightlife, and beachfront luxury, making it the natural home for many of Miami’s most fashionable places to stay.

South Beach is especially famous for its remarkable collection of Art Deco hotels, many of them dating from the 1920s and 1930s. These buildings are protected as part of the area’s architectural heritage, and their pastel façades, geometric details, and vintage glamour help define the character of the neighborhood. In recent years, many of these historic hotels have been carefully renovated and transformed into high-end properties, combining period charm with modern luxury.

Among the best-known examples are The Delano and The Shore Club, both associated with Ian Schrager’s stylish hotel revivals. These properties helped redefine South Beach hospitality by turning classic Art Deco buildings into fashionable destinations with dramatic interiors, sophisticated design, and a strong emphasis on nightlife. They are known not only as hotels but also as social scenes, attracting celebrities, designers, and well-heeled travelers looking for the full Miami experience.

For those seeking an even more luxurious stay, The Setai is one of South Beach’s most exclusive addresses. It combines restored Art Deco architecture with serene Asian-inspired design, creating an atmosphere that is both elegant and understated. With its spacious suites, refined service, and exceptionally high prices, The Setai caters to travelers who want top-tier comfort in one of Miami’s most desirable locations.

A somewhat better-value option is The Standard, which is located not directly on the ocean but on Biscayne Bay. Its setting gives it a quieter, more relaxed atmosphere while still keeping guests close to South Beach. The hotel is particularly well known for its spa facilities, infinity pool, and open-air mud lounge, making it a favorite for visitors who place wellness and relaxation above the beachfront party scene.

This famous stretch of coastline is known not only for its wide sandy beach and energetic nightlife, but also for its remarkable concentration of Art Deco architecture. Many of the area’s hotels are protected historic buildings that have been carefully restored and updated, allowing visitors to enjoy both the glamour of old Miami and the comfort of modern hospitality.

A stay in South Beach can vary widely depending on the hotel’s location, style, amenities, and price. Some properties emphasize fashion, nightlife, and celebrity appeal, while others focus on wellness, privacy, or understated luxury. The best hotels combine the area’s distinctive architectural character with contemporary design, stylish restaurants, pool scenes, and direct access to the beach. For many travelers, choosing the right hotel is central to shaping the entire Miami Beach experience.

Among the most famous names is The Delano, a landmark hotel that helped define South Beach’s modern image as a glamorous, design-led destination. Known for its dramatic interiors, elegant public spaces, and fashionable atmosphere, it attracts guests who want to be close to the social heart of Miami Beach. Similarly, the Shore Club has built its reputation around a lively pool scene, chic design, and a sense of energy that suits visitors looking for a stylish, nightlife-oriented stay.

For travelers seeking a more refined and luxurious experience, The Setai offers a different mood. Combining Art Deco heritage with Asian-inspired design, it is known for spacious rooms, calm service, high-end dining, and an atmosphere of exclusivity. It appeals to guests who want the excitement of South Beach nearby but prefer a quieter, more polished retreat. The Standard, meanwhile, stands out for its focus on wellness and relaxation. Located away from the busiest oceanfront strip, it is especially known for its spa, hydrotherapy facilities, and more laid-back, adults-oriented atmosphere.

These hotels show the range that makes Miami Beach so compelling. A visitor can choose a historic Art Deco property with a buzzing lobby, a beachfront resort with luxury service, a spa-focused escape, or a fashionable hotel surrounded by restaurants, bars, and clubs. Prices vary accordingly, with premium oceanfront and design-led properties commanding higher rates, especially during peak travel periods, while smaller or less centrally located hotels may offer better value.

What unites these options is their connection to Miami’s beachside identity. The city’s hotels are not merely places to sleep; they are part of the attraction itself. Their architecture, pools, restaurants, bars, spas, and social scenes help define the rhythm of a Miami holiday. # Where to Stay in Miami: Best Hotels in South Beach and Beyond

Miami’s hotel scene is as varied as the city itself: Art Deco icons on Ocean Drive, polished beachfront resorts in Mid-Beach, design-forward boutique stays, and sleek high-rises overlooking Biscayne Bay. For many visitors, South Beach remains the main event — close to the sand, nightlife, restaurants, shopping, and some of the city’s most recognizable architecture.

Below are standout Miami hotels to consider, with addresses, typical nightly price ranges, and what kind of traveler each one suits best.

*Prices are approximate and vary widely by season, events, room type, and booking date. Expect higher rates during winter, holidays, Art Basel, Miami Music Week, and major sporting or cultural events.*

---

## Best Hotels in South Beach

### 1. The Setai, Miami Beach  
**Address:** 2001 Collins Ave, Miami Beach, FL 33139  
**Typical price:** About **$900–$2,000+ per night**

A longtime favorite for travelers seeking understated luxury, The Setai blends Asian-inspired design with Miami Beach glamour. Set in the South Beach area but slightly removed from the loudest nightlife corridors, it offers direct beach access, three temperature-controlled pools, spacious suites, and polished service.

**Best for:** Luxury travelers, couples, quiet beachfront stays  
**Why stay here:** Elegant atmosphere, exceptional service, prime Collins Avenue location

---

### 2. 1 Hotel South Beach  
**Address:** 2341 Collins Ave, Miami Beach, FL 33139  
**Typical price:** About **$700–$1,800+ per night**

One of South Beach’s most popular upscale resorts, 1 Hotel South Beach is known for its eco-conscious design, airy rooms, multiple pools, and direct beach access. The rooftop pool and ocean views are major draws, while the hotel’s relaxed luxury style appeals to both couples and families.

**Best for:** Wellness-minded travelers, families, luxury beach vacations  
**Why stay here:** Spacious rooms, rooftop scene, beachfront resort amenities

---

### 3. W South Beach  
**Address:** 2201 Collins Ave, Miami Beach, FL 33139  
**Typical price:** About **$700–$1,700+ per night**

The W South Beach delivers a stylish, energetic stay with large rooms, many offering ocean views and balconies. It’s close to the beach, nightlife, Lincoln Road, and cultural stops like The Bass museum. The scene is fashionable without feeling quite as hectic as Ocean Drive.

**Best for:** Couples, nightlife seekers, design-focused travelers  
**Why stay here:** Big rooms, buzzy atmosphere, prime South Beach address

---

### 4. The Betsy Hotel  
**Address:** 1440 Ocean Dr, Miami Beach, FL 33139  
**Typical price:** About **$350–$900+ per night**

A refined boutique hotel on Ocean Drive, The Betsy offers a more cultured and classic South Beach experience. The property is known for its literary programming, rooftop deck, art-filled interiors, and a location steps from Lummus Park and the beach.

**Best for:** Boutique hotel fans, couples, culture-minded travelers  
**Why stay here:** Historic character, oceanfront location, quieter sophistication

---

### 5. Loews Miami Beach Hotel  
**Address:** 1601 Collins Ave, Miami Beach, FL 33139  
**Typical price:** About **$350–$900+ per night**

Loews is one of the most reliable full-service beachfront hotels in South Beach, especially for travelers who want resort amenities without sacrificing location. It has a large pool area, direct beach access, family-friendly programming, and easy access to Lincoln Road and Ocean Drive.

**Best for:** Families, first-time Miami visitors, resort-style convenience  
**Why stay here:** Central location, beachfront access, dependable service

---

### 6. The Goodtime Hotel  
**Address:** 601 Washington Ave, Miami Beach, FL 33139  
**Typical price:** About **$150–$400+ per night**

Created with a playful, pastel-heavy design aesthetic, The Goodtime Hotel is a lively option a few blocks from the beach. Its pool club and social spaces attract a younger crowd, and the location near Washington Avenue puts guests close to restaurants, bars, and South Beach nightlife.

**Best for:** Younger travelers, groups, budget-conscious style seekers  
**Why stay here:** Fun design, social scene, lower rates than beachfront luxury hotels

---

### 7. Kimpton Surfcomber Hotel  
**Address:** 1717 Collins Ave, Miami Beach, FL 33139  
**Typical price:** About **$250–$650+ per night**

The Kimpton Surfcomber offers a boutique-resort feel in a central South Beach location. It has direct beach access, a lively pool, and the approachable service style Kimpton is known for. It’s a good middle-ground option for travelers who want personality and convenience without ultra-luxury pricing.

**Best for:** Couples, friends, pet owners  
**Why stay here:** Beachfront setting, boutique feel, central location

---

## Best Hotels in Mid-Beach and North Beach

### 8. Faena Hotel Miami Beach  
**Address:** 3201 Collins Ave, Miami Beach, FL 33140  
**Typical price:** About **$800–$2,000+ per night**

Faena is one of Miami’s most theatrical luxury hotels, known for bold interiors, serious dining, and a high-glamour atmosphere. Located in Mid-Beach, it’s close enough to South Beach by taxi or rideshare but removed from the busiest crowds.

**Best for:** Luxury travelers, design lovers, special occasions  
**Why stay here:** Dramatic style, excellent dining, beachfront setting

---

### 9. The Miami Beach EDITION  
**Address:** 2901 Collins Ave, Miami Beach, FL 33140  
**Typical price:** About **$600–$1,500+ per night**

The EDITION brings sleek modern luxury to Mid-Beach, with a beachfront location, stylish rooms, multiple dining options, and nightlife-friendly amenities. It’s polished but relaxed, drawing travelers who want a resort stay with easy access to South Beach.

**Best for:** Couples, upscale leisure travelers, nightlife fans  
**Why stay here:** Chic design, beachfront access, strong food and beverage options

---

### 10. Fontainebleau Miami Beach  
**Address:** 4441 Collins Ave, Miami Beach, FL 33140  
**Typical price:** About **$350–$1,000+ per night**

A Miami Beach landmark, the Fontainebleau is big, bold, and built for travelers who want a full resort experience. Expect multiple pools, restaurants, bars, nightlife, and a constant sense of activity. It’s north of South Beach, so plan on rideshares if most of your itinerary is centered around Ocean Drive or Lincoln Road.

**Best for:** Resort lovers, groups, nightlife travelers  
**Why stay here:** Iconic Miami history, large-scale amenities, high-energy atmosphere

---

## Best Hotels in Downtown Miami and Brickell

### 11. EAST Miami  
**Address:** 788 Brickell Plaza, Miami, FL 33131  
**Typical price:** About **$300–$700+ per night**

For travelers who prefer city views over beach access, EAST Miami is a strong Brickell choice. Connected to the Brickell City Centre complex, it offers easy access to shopping, dining, rooftop bars, and the financial district. The beach is a drive away, but the urban convenience is hard to beat.

**Best for:** Business travelers, food lovers, city-break visitors  
**Why stay here:** Great Brickell location, modern rooms, rooftop bar scene

---

### 12. Mandarin Oriental, Miami  
**Address:** 500 Brickell Key Dr, Miami, FL 33131  
**Typical price:** About **$450–$1,200+ per night**

Located on Brickell Key, the Mandarin Oriental offers a calmer waterfront stay with sweeping views of Biscayne Bay and the Miami skyline. It’s not a beach hotel, but it delivers polished luxury, a quieter atmosphere, and easy access to Brickell and Downtown Miami.

**Best for:** Couples, business travelers, luxury travelers seeking quiet  
**Why stay here:** Waterfront views, refined service, peaceful location near Brickell

---

## How to Choose the Right Miami Hotel

**Stay in South Beach if:**  
You want to be near the beach, Ocean Drive, nightlife, Art Deco architecture, Lincoln Road, and a walkable vacation atmosphere.

**Stay in Mid-Beach if:**  
You want a more resort-focused stay with bigger properties, fewer crowds, and easy rideshare access to South Beach.

**Stay in Brickell or Downtown if:**  
You’re visiting for business, dining, shopping, museums, concerts, or cruises — and don’t mind driving to the beach.

**Stay in North Beach if:**  
You want a quieter, more residential beach experience, often at lower prices than South Beach or Mid-Beach.

---

## Quick Picks

- **Best luxury hotel in South Beach:** The Setai, Miami Beach  
- **Best eco-chic resort:** 1 Hotel South Beach  
- **Best boutique stay:** The Betsy Hotel  
- **Best for families:** Loews Miami Beach Hotel  
- **Best for nightlife:** W South Beach or Fontainebleau Miami Beach  
- **Best stylish value:** The Goodtime Hotel  
- **Best Brickell stay:** EAST Miami  
- **Best quiet luxury:** Mandarin Oriental, Miami  

---

## Reader Question

Have you stayed at a hotel in Miami or South Beach that deserves a spot on this list? Share your favorite property, what you paid, and what made the stay memorable in the comments.

## Where to stay in Miami

Miami’s hotel scene runs from high-gloss beachfront resorts to restored Art Deco gems and characterful budget stays. For first-timers, South Beach offers the classic Miami experience; Mid-Beach is more resort-like and relaxed; Brickell and Downtown suit nightlife, dining and business; Coral Gables is elegant, leafy and quieter.

### Glamorous beach hotels

**Faena Hotel Miami Beach — Mid-Beach**  
A theatrical, ultra-glamorous oceanfront hotel with red-and-gold interiors, Damien Hirst art, polished service and a see-and-be-seen pool scene. Best for a decadent Miami stay.

**The Miami Beach EDITION — Mid-Beach**  
Sleek, modern and stylish, with beachfront access, a beautiful pool area, buzzy restaurants and a basement entertainment space with bowling and an ice-skating rink.

**W South Beach — South Beach**  
A glossy all-suite beachfront hotel with large rooms, ocean views, a lively pool scene and easy access to South Beach restaurants and nightlife.

### Art Deco properties

**The Betsy — South Beach**  
One of Ocean Drive’s most refined addresses, combining Art Deco charm with a quieter, cultured atmosphere. Expect elegant rooms, a rooftop pool, live music and a great location by the beach.

**National Hotel Miami Beach — South Beach**  
A classic 1939 Art Deco hotel with a strikingly long pool, vintage glamour and direct beach access. Adults-only, making it a calmer South Beach option.

**Esme Miami Beach — Española Way**  
A stylish revival of historic buildings near Española Way, with Mediterranean-inspired design, a rooftop pool and a more intimate feel than the big beachfront hotels.

### Boutique options

**Life House, Little Havana — Little Havana**  
A charming boutique stay inspired by Miami’s Cuban heritage, with tropical interiors and a location that’s ideal for exploring Calle Ocho.

**The Local House — South of Fifth**  
A relaxed boutique hotel in one of South Beach’s most desirable pockets, close to the beach but away from the loudest nightlife.

**Urbanica The Euclid — South Beach**  
Minimal, modern and well-priced for the area, with a boutique feel and a good South of Fifth location near restaurants and the beach.

### Luxury stays

**Four Seasons Hotel at The Surf Club — Surfside**  
One of the most elegant hotels in the Miami area, set in a legendary private club with serene interiors, excellent dining, oceanfront pools and polished service.

**Mandarin Oriental, Miami — Brickell Key**  
A sophisticated waterfront hotel on a quiet island just off Brickell, with skyline views, a private beach-style lounge area and easy access to Downtown and Brickell dining.

**1 Hotel South Beach — South Beach**  
A luxurious eco-minded resort with huge rooms, natural materials, multiple pools, a rooftop bar and direct beach access.

### Spa hotels

**Carillon Miami Wellness Resort — North Beach**  
A serious wellness-focused hotel with one of Miami’s most extensive spa and fitness offerings, including thermal circuits, treatment rooms and wellness programming.

**The Setai, Miami Beach — South Beach**  
A serene, Asian-inspired luxury hotel with three temperature-controlled pools, a tranquil spa and superb beachfront service.

**Acqualina Resort & Residences — Sunny Isles Beach**  
A grand, Mediterranean-style oceanfront resort known for its spa, spacious rooms, family-friendly luxury and polished service.

### Quirky budget choices

**Freehand Miami — Mid-Beach**

**Biltmore Hotel Miami Coral Gables — Coral Gables**

## Miami sleeps: Six stylish hotels for a South Florida escape

Miami has always been more than a beach town. It is a mood — all white sand and neon, late dinners and early swims, art deco curves and tropical swagger. For travelers looking to make a hotel part of the story, the city offers everything from landmark glamour to spa-focused serenity.

Rates in Miami vary dramatically by season, especially around Art Basel, winter holidays and major events. The figures below are approximate starting rates for a double room, before taxes and resort fees, and should be checked directly with the hotel before booking.

### The Delano South Beach  
**Best for:** Iconic Miami glamour  
**Approximate double-room rate:** From about **$400–$700+** per night, depending on season and reopening status  

Few hotels are as closely tied to the image of modern South Beach as The Delano. Known for its soaring lobby, billowing white curtains and Philippe Starck-designed minimalism, the property helped define Miami’s 1990s hotel renaissance. Travelers should check current availability and renovation/reopening details, but when operating, The Delano is the kind of place visitors book as much for the mythology as the mattress.

### Shore Club South Beach  
**Best for:** A fashionable Collins Avenue address  
**Approximate double-room rate:** Historically from about **$350–$600+** per night; check current status  

Another name from South Beach’s boutique-hotel golden era, Shore Club has long been associated with sleek design, nightlife energy and a prime location just steps from the sand. The property has undergone periods of redevelopment, so would-be guests should confirm whether rooms are available during their travel dates. If open, it appeals to travelers who want a stylish base close to restaurants, beach clubs and the after-dark pulse of Miami Beach.

### The Setai, Miami Beach  
**Best for:** High-end calm and oceanfront luxury  
**Approximate double-room rate:** From about **$800–$1,500+** per night  

The Setai is Miami Beach for travelers who prefer their glamour hushed rather than loud. Set in a restored art deco building with a striking modern tower, the hotel blends Asian-inspired design with beachfront resort polish. Expect polished service, serene pools, spacious rooms and a sense of privacy that feels rare on Collins Avenue. It is one of the city’s most luxurious stays, with prices to match.

### The Standard Spa, Miami Beach  
**Best for:** Wellness, bay views and a social scene  
**Approximate double-room rate:** From about **$300–$600+** per night  

On Belle Isle, just off the Venetian Causeway, The Standard trades oceanfront spectacle for Biscayne Bay breezes and a laid-back spa culture. Guests come for the hammam, hydrotherapy, yoga, mud lounge, waterfront pool and sunset drinks that feel more local than touristy. Rooms are simple and retro-cool, but the real draw is the communal, health-meets-hedonism atmosphere.

### Pelican Hotel  
**Best for:** Art deco character on Ocean Drive  
**Approximate double-room rate:** From about **$180–$350+** per night  

For travelers who want South Beach personality without the mega-resort feel, the Pelican is a longtime Ocean Drive favorite. The boutique property, known for individually themed rooms and playful design, sits directly across from the beach and in the thick of the art deco district. It is quirky, compact and well placed — a good choice for guests who plan to spend more time exploring than lounging behind resort gates.

### The Biltmore Hotel, Coral Gables  
**Best for:** Historic grandeur away from South Beach  
**Approximate double-room rate:** From about **$300–$600+** per night  

A Miami classic, The Biltmore rises over Coral Gables with Mediterranean Revival drama, a landmark tower and one of the most famous hotel pools in Florida. Opened in the 1920s, it offers a different version of Miami luxury: golf, grand architecture, leafy boulevards and old-world elegance rather than beachfront buzz. It is especially appealing for travelers who want proximity to Coral Gables, Coconut Grove and the airport while staying somewhere with a strong sense of history.

### Choosing the right Miami stay

For scene and legend, look to **The Delano** or **Shore Club**, provided current operations align with your dates. For polished oceanfront indulgence, **The Setai** is the splurge. For wellness and sunsets, **The Standard** is hard to beat. For art deco charm and relative value, **Pelican Hotel** delivers a classic South Beach address. And for travelers who prefer historic elegance over beach-club energy, **The Biltmore** offers one of Miami’s most atmospheric stays.

### Where to Stay in Miami: South Beach Style, Collins Avenue Classics, and Resort Relaxation

Miami’s hotel scene is as vibrant as the city itself, blending beachfront luxury, Art Deco glamour, late-night energy, and spa-worthy serenity. For travelers who want to be in the heart of it all, South Beach remains the classic choice. This iconic neighborhood is famous for its pastel-colored Art Deco buildings, a historic architectural legacy from the 1920s and 1930s that still gives Ocean Drive and the surrounding streets their signature look. Staying here means waking up close to the beach, cafés, boutique shops, and some of Miami’s most recognizable scenery.

Collins Avenue is one of the best places to begin your hotel search. Stretching through South Beach and beyond, it’s lined with everything from stylish boutique hotels to grand oceanfront resorts. Many Collins Avenue hotels offer easy beach access, rooftop pools, chic lounges, and interiors that reflect Miami’s mix of tropical ease and modern design. Whether you’re looking for a romantic weekend, a friends’ getaway, or a full-service resort experience, this area puts you close to the action.

After dark, Miami comes alive. South Beach is known for its nightlife, with cocktail bars, hotel lounges, dance clubs, and live music venues all within easy reach. Many hotels double as social hubs, hosting pool parties, DJ nights, and elegant lobby bars perfect for a pre-dinner drink. If relaxation is more your style, Miami’s top hotels also feature impressive spas offering massages, facials, steam rooms, and wellness treatments inspired by the ocean and the tropics.

Dining is another major reason to choose your hotel carefully. From upscale restaurants led by celebrity chefs to casual beachfront spots serving ceviche, Cuban classics, and fresh seafood, Miami’s accommodations often place you steps from memorable meals. Some hotels even house destination restaurants worth visiting whether or not you’re staying overnight.

Have a favorite Miami hotel, hidden gem, or unforgettable South Beach stay? Share your top pick and help fellow travelers find the perfect place to check in.

# Where to Stay in Miami: Best Neighborhoods and Hotels for Every Kind of Trip

Miami is not one destination so much as a constellation: Art Deco glamour on South Beach, design-forward luxury in Mid-Beach, a buzzing creative scene in Wynwood, sleek towers in Brickell and family-friendly calm in Coconut Grove and Coral Gables. Choosing where to stay will shape your trip as much as your dinner reservations or beach plans.

Below, find a neighborhood-by-neighborhood guide to Miami’s best areas to stay, with standout hotels, typical starting rates, signature amenities and who each area suits best.

*Note: Prices are approximate starting nightly rates and can vary significantly by season, events, holidays and room type.*

---

## South Beach: Best for First-Timers, Nightlife and Classic Miami

South Beach is the postcard version of Miami: pastel Art Deco hotels, oceanfront promenades, late-night restaurants and a see-and-be-seen beach scene. Stay here if you want to walk to the sand, bars, cafés and clubs — and don’t mind a little buzz after dark.

### The Betsy – South Beach  
**Location:** Ocean Drive, South Beach  
**Typical rates:** From about **$350–$600 per night**  
**Best for:** Culture lovers, couples, boutique-hotel fans  

A refined Ocean Drive address with literary charm, The Betsy feels more grown-up than its neon-lit neighbors. Expect colonial-style architecture, a rooftop pool, live music and one of the more elegant atmospheres in South Beach.

**Amenities include:**  
- Rooftop pool and ocean views  
- On-site dining and bar  
- Wellness programming  
- Pet-friendly rooms  
- Easy beach access  

### The Setai, Miami Beach  
**Location:** Collins Avenue, South Beach  
**Typical rates:** From about **$800–$1,500+ per night**  
**Best for:** Luxury travelers, honeymooners, spa weekends  

One of Miami Beach’s most polished luxury hotels, The Setai blends Asian-inspired design with Art Deco bones. Its three temperature-controlled pools, serene spa and beachfront service make it a top choice for travelers seeking calm amid the South Beach energy.

**Amenities include:**  
- Three outdoor pools  
- Beach loungers and service  
- Spa and wellness facilities  
- Fine dining  
- Spacious suites and ocean views  

### Life House, South of Fifth  
**Location:** South of Fifth, Miami Beach  
**Typical rates:** From about **$180–$350 per night**  
**Best for:** Stylish stays, value-conscious couples, quieter South Beach trips  

South of Fifth is still South Beach, but with a more residential, local feel. Life House offers a design-forward stay in one of the area’s prettiest pockets, close to the beach, South Pointe Park and some of Miami’s best restaurants.

**Amenities include:**  
- Boutique interiors  
- Restaurant and bar  
- Walkable South of Fifth location  
- Easy access to beach and dining  

**Nearby:** Explore the city’s most famous stretch of sand in our guide to **[Miami’s best beaches](/travel/miami/best-beaches)**, then plan dinner with **[where to eat in Miami](/travel/miami/best-restaurants)**.

---

## Mid-Beach: Best for Resorts, Beach Clubs and a Stylish Escape

Just north of South Beach, Mid-Beach is where Miami shifts into resort mode. The hotels are larger, the pools more dramatic and the pace slightly less frantic. It’s ideal if you want beach access, great dining and a glamorous hotel scene without being in the thick of Ocean Drive.

### Faena Hotel Miami Beach  
**Location:** Collins Avenue, Mid-Beach  
**Typical rates:** From about **$900–$1,800+ per night**  
**Best for:** Design lovers, special occasions, maximalist luxury  

Faena is theatrical in the best possible way: red velvet, gold accents, Damien Hirst artwork and an unmistakable sense of drama. The hotel anchors the Faena District, with destination dining, a striking theater and one of Miami’s most distinctive pool scenes.

**Amenities include:**  
- Oceanfront pool and beach club  
- Tierra Santa Healing House spa  
- Destination restaurants and bars  
- Live entertainment and cultural programming  
- Lavish rooms and suites  

### The Miami Beach EDITION  
**Location:** Collins Avenue, Mid-Beach  
**Typical rates:** From about **$500–$1,000+ per night**  
**Best for:** Couples, design-minded travelers, nightlife without chaos  

Sleek, understated and cool, The EDITION brings Ian Schrager polish to a beachfront setting. By day, guests drift between the pool, beach and spa; by night, the hotel’s bars and entertainment spaces keep things lively without requiring a taxi to South Beach.

**Amenities include:**  
- Beachfront location  
- Two pools  
- Spa and fitness center  
- Restaurants and bars  
- Basement entertainment venue with bowling and skating  

### Fontainebleau Miami Beach  
**Location:** Collins Avenue, Mid-Beach  
**Typical rates:** From about **$350–$800+ per night**  
**Best for:** Groups, nightlife, resort amenities  

A Miami icon since the 1950s, Fontainebleau is big, bold and built for travelers who want everything on-site: pools, restaurants, nightlife, beach service and a high-energy lobby scene. It’s especially popular for group trips and long weekends.

**Amenities include:**  
- Multiple pools and cabanas  
- Beach access  
- Spa and fitness center  
- Numerous restaurants and bars  
- On-site nightclub  

**Nearby:** Pair a resort stay with a culture hit using our guide to **[the best things to do in Miami](/travel/miami/things-to-do)**.

---

## Surfside and Bal Harbour: Best for Quiet Luxury and Shopping

North of Miami Beach, Surfside and Bal Harbour offer a calmer coastal base. The beach is still beautiful, but the scene is more polished and residential. Stay here for luxury hotels, designer shopping and a slower rhythm.

### Four Seasons Hotel at The Surf Club  
**Location:** Surfside  
**Typical rates:** From about **$1,000–$2,000+ per night**  
**Best for:** Ultra-luxury, couples, quiet beach vacations  

Set in a legendary private club that once hosted Hollywood royalty, Four Seasons at The Surf Club is one of the area’s most sophisticated stays. It’s elegant without feeling flashy, with expansive oceanfront grounds and a deeply restorative atmosphere.

**Amenities include:**  
- Oceanfront pools  
- Beach service  
- Spa and wellness offerings  
- Fine dining  
- Elegant rooms, suites and residences  

### The St. Regis Bal Harbour Resort  
**Location:** Bal Harbour  
**Typical rates:** From about **$900–$1,700+ per night**  
**Best for:** Shoppers, luxury travelers, families seeking space  

Directly across from Bal Harbour Shops, The St. Regis pairs polished service with large rooms and oceanfront views. It’s a strong choice for travelers who want high-end shopping, a quieter beach and resort comforts in one place.

**Amenities include:**  
- Oceanfront pools  
- Remède Spa  
- Butler service  
- Family-friendly programming  
- Proximity to Bal Harbour Shops  

**Nearby:** Make time for retail therapy with our guide to **[shopping in Miami](/travel/miami/shopping)**.

---

## Brickell and Downtown Miami: Best for Business, Dining and City Views

Brickell is Miami’s financial district, but after dark it becomes one of the city’s busiest dining and cocktail hubs. Downtown, meanwhile, puts you close to museums, arenas, Biscayne Bay and the Metromover. Stay here if you prefer skyline views to beachfront lounging — or if you’re planning to explore beyond Miami Beach.

### EAST Miami  
**Location:** Brickell City Centre, Brickell  
**Typical rates:** From about **$250–$500 per night**  
**Best for:** Business travelers, shoppers, dining-focused trips  

Rising above Brickell City Centre, EAST Miami has a modern, international feel and some of the neighborhood’s best views. Rooms feature balconies, while the rooftop bar draws a local crowd for sunset cocktails.

**Amenities include:**  
- Rooftop bar  
- Outdoor pool deck  
- Fitness center  
- Direct access to Brickell City Centre  
- Balcony rooms with skyline or bay views  

### SLS LUX Brickell  
**Location:** Brickell  
**Typical rates:** From about **$250–$550 per night**  
**Best for:** Nightlife, long weekends, travelers who want apartment-style space  

SLS LUX brings a playful, design-heavy sensibility to central Brickell. Rooms and suites often feel residential, and the location places guests within walking distance of restaurants, bars and shopping.

**Amenities include:**  
- Rooftop pool  
- Spa and fitness center  
- On-site dining  
- Spacious rooms and suites  
- Walkable Brickell location  

### Kimpton EPIC Hotel  
**Location:** Downtown Miami, near the Miami River  
**Typical rates:** From about **$250–$500 per night**  
**Best for:** Bay views, business trips, cruises and downtown events  

The Kimpton EPIC is a convenient downtown option with water views, a lively pool deck and easy access to Brickell, Bayfront Park, Kaseya Center and PortMiami. It’s a particularly practical choice before or after a cruise.

**Amenities include:**  
- Two rooftop pools  
- Spa and wellness center  
- Restaurants and bars  
- Pet-friendly policy  
- Close to PortMiami and downtown attractions  

**Nearby:** For museums, waterfront walks and live events, see **[downtown Miami attractions](/travel/miami/downtown-guide)**.

---

## Wynwood and the Design District: Best for Art, Nightlife and Boutique Energy

Wynwood is Miami’s mural-covered playground, packed with galleries, breweries, coffee shops and late-night venues. Just north, the Design District is sleeker, with luxury boutiques, public art and excellent restaurants. This area suits travelers who want a more urban, creative stay — and don’t need to be right on the beach.

### Arlo Wynwood  
**Location:** Wynwood  
**Typical rates:** From about **$180–$350 per night**  
**Best for:** Art lovers, younger travelers, weekend escapes  

Arlo Wynwood puts guests in the heart of Miami’s street-art district, with a rooftop pool, playful design and easy access to galleries, bars and restaurants. It’s one of the best hotel options if Wynwood is your main focus.

**Amenities include:**  
- Rooftop pool and bar  
- Fitness center  
- On-site dining  
- Art-forward design  
- Walkable Wynwood location  

### Hyde Midtown Miami  
**Location:** Midtown Miami, near Design District and Wynwood  
**Typical rates:** From about **$180–$400 per night**  
**Best for:** Longer stays, shoppers, nightlife  

Hyde Midtown offers a residential-style stay between Wynwood and the Design District. Many rooms have balconies and kitchenettes, making it useful for travelers who want more space while staying near Miami’s creative core.

**Amenities include:**  
- Pool deck  
- Fitness center  
- Tennis court  
- Balcony rooms  
- Access to Midtown, Wynwood and Design District  

**Nearby:** Start with our guide to **[Wynwood’s best galleries, murals and bars](/travel/miami/wynwood-guide)**.

---

## Coconut Grove: Best for Families, Green Space and a Village Feel

Coconut Grove is one of Miami’s oldest neighborhoods, with leafy streets, bayfront parks, marinas and a relaxed village atmosphere. It’s a strong choice for families, couples and repeat visitors who want a quieter stay with easy access to Coral Gables and downtown.

### Mr. C Miami – Coconut Grove  
**Location:** Coconut Grove  
**Typical rates:** From about **$300–$600 per night**  
**Best for:** Couples, boutique luxury, bay views  

With a nautical, Italian-inspired sensibility, Mr. C brings polished service and a breezy rooftop scene to Coconut Grove. Rooms are elegant and many have balconies overlooking Biscayne Bay or the neighborhood canopy.

**Amenities include:**  
- Rooftop pool  
- Bellini restaurant  
- Spa and fitness center  
- Balcony rooms  
- Walkable Coconut Grove location  

### The Ritz-Carlton Coconut Grove, Miami  
**Location:** Coconut Grove  
**Typical rates:** From about **$350–$700+ per night**  
**Best for:** Families, business travelers, quiet luxury  

A calm alternative to the beach hotels, The Ritz-Carlton Coconut Grove offers spacious rooms, a tranquil pool area and easy access to parks, marinas and neighborhood restaurants. It’s especially appealing for travelers who want comfort without South Beach commotion.

**Amenities include:**  
- Outdoor pool  
- Spa and fitness center  
- Restaurant and bar  
- Family-friendly rooms  
- Close to Biscayne Bay and Coconut Grove dining  

**Nearby:** Plan a slower day with **[family-friendly things to do in Miami](/travel/miami/family-friendly)**.

---

## Coral Gables: Best for Romance, Architecture and a Quieter Base

Coral Gables feels like a Mediterranean fantasy transplanted to South Florida, with banyan-lined streets, historic landmarks and elegant restaurants. It’s not on the beach, but it offers a sophisticated base close to Coconut Grove, Little Havana and Miami International Airport.

### Biltmore Hotel Miami Coral Gables  
**Location:** Coral Gables  
**Typical rates:** From about **$300–$650 per night**  
**Best for:** History lovers, golf, romantic weekends  

A grand 1920s landmark, The Biltmore is one of Miami’s most storied hotels. With a striking tower, lush grounds, a massive pool and an old-world sense of occasion, it feels worlds away from the high-rise energy of Miami Beach.

**Amenities include:**  
- Historic architecture  
- Large resort-style pool  
- Golf course  
- Spa and fitness center  
- Fine dining and afternoon tea  

### Hotel Colonnade Coral Gables, Autograph Collection  
**Location:** Miracle Mile, Coral Gables  
**Typical rates:** From about **$200–$450 per night**  
**Best for:** Walkability, dining, business travelers  

Set on Miracle Mile, Hotel Colonnade is well placed for restaurants, shops and Coral Gables’ leafy streets. It’s a practical yet stylish option for travelers who want a central mainland stay.

**Amenities include:**  
- Rooftop pool  
- Fitness center  
- On-site dining  
- Walkable location  
- Event and meeting spaces  

**Nearby:** Add a food-focused afternoon with our guide to **[Little Havana and Miami’s best neighborhoods](/travel/miami/neighborhoods)**.

---

## Key Biscayne: Best for Beach Calm and Outdoor Escapes

A short drive from mainland Miami, Key Biscayne offers a quieter, more nature-focused beach stay. It’s ideal for travelers who want tennis, biking, kayaking, family-friendly beaches and a resort atmosphere removed from the city’s party circuit.

### The Ritz-Carlton Key Biscayne, Miami  
**Location:** Key Biscayne  
**Typical rates:** From about **$450–$900+ per night**  
**Best for:** Families, beach vacations, tennis and outdoor activities  

This oceanfront resort has a relaxed island feel, with spacious grounds, tennis courts and easy access to Crandon Park and Bill Baggs Cape Florida State Park. It’s one of the best Miami-area choices for families who want beach time without South Beach crowds.

**Amenities include:**  
- Beachfront location  
- Multiple pools  
- Tennis center  
- Spa and fitness center  
- Family-friendly programming  
- Restaurants and bars  

**Nearby:** See where to swim, paddle and bike in **[Miami’s best outdoor activities](/travel/miami/outdoors)**.

---

## Best Area to Stay in Miami by Trip Type

**For first-time visitors:** South Beach  
You’ll be close to the beach, Art Deco architecture, nightlife and classic Miami sights.

**For luxury:** Surfside, Bal Harbour or Mid-Beach  
Choose Four Seasons at The Surf Club, St. Regis Bal Harbour, Faena or The Setai.

**For nightlife:** South Beach, Mid-Beach or Brickell  
South Beach is the classic choice; Brickell is better for cocktail bars and restaurants.

**For families:** Key Biscayne, Coconut Grove or Bal Harbour  
These areas offer calmer settings, bigger rooms and easier access to parks or quieter beaches.

**For business travelers:** Brickell or Downtown  
Stay near offices, restaurants, transit and PortMiami.

**For art and culture:** Wynwood, Design District or South Beach  
Wynwood is best for galleries and murals; South Beach is best for architecture.

**For a quieter romantic trip:** Coconut Grove, Coral Gables or Surfside  
Expect leafy streets, refined restaurants and a slower pace.

---

## Booking Tips for Miami Hotels

- **High season runs roughly December through April**, when sunny weather and major events push rates higher.  
- **Art Basel Miami Beach in December** brings some of the year’s most expensive hotel prices.  
- **Summer can offer better deals**, though humidity, storms and hurricane-season considerations apply.  
- **Resort fees are common**, especially in Miami Beach; check what they include before booking.  
- **Parking can be expensive**, often $40–$60 or more per night at luxury hotels.  
- **If you won’t have a car**, South Beach, Brickell, Wynwood and Coconut Grove are among the more walkable bases.
